explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/94: n points in convex position with distinct distances u_1, ..., u_t, u_i occurring f(u_i) times; then Σ f(u_i)^2 ≪ n^3 (Erdős credits Fishburn; Lefmann–Thiele proved it under the weaker no-three-collinear hypothesis). The statement gives an absolute C > 0 with Σ_{u ∈ distanceSet P} f(u)^2 <= C|P|^3 for every `ConvexIndep` finite P ⊆ ℝ². `distanceSet` is the set of distances over distinct pairs, and `distanceMultiplicity` counts unordered pairs (ordered off-diagonal pairs divided by 2), consistent with the proved test Σ f(u) = C(n,2). `ConvexIndep` (no point in the convex hull of the others) is the standard reading of 'determine a convex polygon'; in any case it implies no three collinear, so the statement follows from the Lefmann–Thiele variant.
